subject.title: [Feature]: Structured Callback Actions and Thread Context Inheritance for Agent Handoffs

question: What public A2A handoff contract should OpenClaw expose for structured skip/no-reply outcomes and announce routing: a `sessions_send` action/override shape, the broader `announceTarget` contract, or a single combined protocol?
rationale: The missing behavior is real in source, but the fix adds public tool semantics and overlaps active A2A routing/dispatch design issues, so automation should not choose the API shape alone.

options.title: Sponsor a typed A2A contract
options.body: Add structured skip/no-reply outcome parameters and thread-aware announce routing in one backward-compatible contract with focused tests for legacy token behavior.

options.title: Fold this into announceTarget
options.body: Keep this issue open only as acceptance coverage while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/27445 owns the public routing API and implementation plan.

options.title: Keep legacy tokens only
options.body: Decline new public tool surface and document exact-token behavior plus current thread fallback fixes as the supported path.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a typed A2A contract
recommendation.body: Add structured skip/no-reply outcome parameters and thread-aware announce routing in one backward-compatible contract with focused tests for legacy token behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He has already scoped the related handoff protocol work and appears in the current sessions/A2A history for the central files.
